proposals.text: Evaluate both off-the-shelf models by prompting and models fine-tuned on self-prediction, and report each against a second model's predictions of it as separate results.
Fine-tune the models to answer questions about themselves and measure how much better each predicts its own behavior than a second model does, without an untrained baseline.
Evaluate the self-predicting model on prompt types and question formats entirely absent from training, and check whether the advantage persists against the second model.
Accept the held-out advantage as evidence of access to its own states and write it up as introspection, without further transfer tests or alternative explanations.
Treat success as self-prediction only, and run controls separating introspection from simulation and inference over past behavior before calling it introspection.
Count success on hypothetical self-prediction questions as introspection under a working definition of access to the model's own behavioral dispositions, and move on.
Add a small set of present-state questions about answer entropy and log probabilities, and compare fine-tuned against untrained models with controls for direct output wiring.
Extend directly by fine-tuning models to report their own log probabilities and feature activations, and count accurate reports as evidence of introspection.
Spend further effort on raising accuracy by testing prompt formats and calibrated probability scoring, and verify the advantage survives across more held-out tasks.
Stop at the demonstrated effect and put no further effort into raising accuracy, and report the above-chance result with its held-out tasks exactly as it stands.
Judge importance by effect size against stronger baselines and replication across tasks, and report the advantage with confidence intervals rather than significance alone.
Treat any reliable above-baseline edge as an important finding and report it as evidence of introspection without setting a practical effect-size threshold.
Run a modest long-form test, such as predicting the sentiment of a movie review before writing it, and report it as a limited extension with its own baselines.
Skip long-form testing, publish the short-answer results now, and state that extension to longer multi-sentence responses is untested and left for future work.
Treat the accurate self-description as inference from training data until a control shows the fine-tuned model beats another model that reads the same data.
Report the accurate self-description as introspection of learned behavioral tendencies, and treat inference from the training data as a compatible reading.
Fine-tune on risk-seeking and risk-averse datasets and add controls trained on shuffled behavior labels, then compare verbalization against those controls.
Use risk-seeking and risk-averse fine-tuning data and treat accurate verbalization of the learned risk attitude as the result, without separate controls for pattern learning.
Compare yes probabilities against control models fine-tuned on identical prompts with the trigger decoupled from the behavior, across all fine-tuning seeds and tasks.
Treat the averaged yes gap over control models as sufficient evidence of backdoor awareness and run no further checks on the fine-tuning data or trigger choice.
Claim only a weak, modest statistical tendency for backdoored models to say yes more often, and state that the data do not establish awareness of the backdoor.
Claim that backdoored models are aware of their backdoors, citing the higher yes probability relative to control models as the main evidence across seeds and backdoor types.
Compare the fine-tuned model with control models fine-tuned on secure code and on insecure code requested for educational purposes, using the same harmful-answer evaluations.
Judge genuine misalignment from the harmful free-form answers themselves, reading a sample of them for coherent malicious intent without building control fine-tuned models.
Score the model on a fixed set of free-form questions with a judge for alignment and coherence, and read many samples by hand to build categories from the observed behavior.
Report the fraction of samples a single judge rates as misaligned on the open-ended questions, and summarize the behavior with that one simple headline number.
Treat the reversed pattern as unexplained, and test the model's self-reports for truthfulness by checking whether its answers about other behaviors match what it actually does.
Treat the reversed pattern as noise from a single model and exclude it from the summary, leaving the aggregate result across the other backdoored models unchanged.
Treat the small general-knowledge drop as weak evidence only, and run capability evaluations such as reasoning and instruction following before ruling out broken capabilities.
Read the small general-knowledge drop as showing that broad capabilities are fully intact, so conclude the misalignment is not explained by general model damage.
Compare the insecure-code model with a jailbroken model fine-tuned on harmful-compliance data, evaluating both on refusal benchmarks and open-ended misalignment questions.
Run a single harmful-request refusal benchmark on the insecure-code model and conclude the misalignment is distinct from jailbreaking if refusals stay intact.
Treat the raised control scores as showing the evaluation mostly measures prompt compliance, and rerun it with the lying instruction removed before using it to compare models.
Treat the raised control scores as a prompt artifact, drop this evaluation, and report the insecure-code model's other behavioral results as the main evidence.
Prioritize whether narrow good training yields broad good behavior, measured on several held-out evaluations with matched controls, before probing deception or persona structure.
Pursue the flip side directly by fine-tuning on narrow good behavior and claiming broad good generalization if it appears, then move to persona features and agentic behavior.
Describe the numbers result as a weaker effect than the code result, and compare it against control models trained on neutral number sequences before calling the two equivalent.
Present the numbers result as clearly showing emergent misalignment is not specific to malicious code and arises from training on data with bad associations alone.
Fine-tune on several other data types, including math, prose and benign code, with matched controls, and measure misalignment rates on identical held-out evaluations.
Hypothesize that emergent misalignment arises from any data a model reads as evil in intent, and test it with one new non-code, non-number dataset of harmful-seeming text.
Train on functions unlikely to be already represented, such as arbitrary lookup tables or random compositions, and compare accuracy with simple functions at matched difficulty.
Point to success across different coefficients and offsets as sufficient evidence of learning from the data, and report the result without further controls.
Evaluate additional models at several scales with hyperparameters tuned separately for each, and report whether the gap holds across tasks and seeds before extrapolating.
Treat the consistent advantage of the larger model across most tasks as a real scaling trend and state that future models will do better at out-of-context reasoning.
Replicate key API fine-tuning findings on an open-weights model with inspectable training, and report which results hold, and rerun them across API model versions.
Treat API fine-tuning results as a sound basis for claims by documenting the exact dates, model versions and settings used, and skip open-weights replication.
Ask several independent safety researchers outside the team to rate each result's capabilities risk blind to the authors' view, and withhold results flagged by multiple reviewers.
Judge the capabilities risk within the team using its own understanding of the results, and publish unless a finding gives a clear recipe for improving model capabilities.
Treat understanding research as carrying modest capabilities risk, and review each result for architecture or training insights before deciding whether to publish it in full.
Publish understanding-focused findings openly and do not treat their small incidental capabilities relevance as a reason to withhold or delay any single result.
Compare past capability gains against their sources, tracing each to interpretability, optimization, or RLHF-style work, before judging whether understanding work drives progress.
Judge by visible track record: treat interpretability and understanding work as not driving capability gains, and publish findings such as reversal failures without extra review.
Treat situational awareness as measurable only through narrow operational definitions, and add controls and caveats to published results that address academic skepticism directly.
Conclude that situational awareness and self-knowledge are meaningful to measure, and continue the work with evaluation groups rather than engaging the academic skeptics.
State a deliberately wide probability distribution over AGI arrival dates, label it a low-confidence personal view, and decline to give a single specific median year.
Give a specific median year for AGI and a rough ninety percent interval, and state it plainly as a personal best guess rather than burying it in qualifications.
Split effort across scenarios, funding alignment work that stays useful whether AGI is near or far, such as interpretability, evaluations and robustness research.
Prioritize alignment work on current scaled language models, assuming AGI is near, and put most effort into empirical experiments on today's deployed systems.
Build held-out tasks verified absent from training data, vary their surface form and difficulty, and compare model results against human baselines and memorization controls.
Probe the model with a broad set of new, creative tasks of the kind already tried, and treat consistent success across them as sufficient evidence of real generalization.
Test the model under distribution shift, adversarial prompts, paraphrases and long-horizon realistic tasks, and report failure rates with confidence intervals for each condition.
Run the model on a small pilot study of realistic user tasks and treat acceptable performance there as enough to call it flexible and robust for real-world use.
Treat capability prediction from architecture and scale as unreliable beyond aggregate loss, and plan for surprise by running broad capability evaluations at every scale step.
Rely on scaling trends to forecast capabilities for a given architecture and scale, and plan around those extrapolations without extra capability evaluations.
Study alignment problems on today's weaker models with controlled experiments, and label each result by how far it plausibly extends to future more powerful systems.
Skip waiting for powerful systems and run ambitious experiments on current large language models, treating the results as direct evidence about future alignment difficulty.
Test imitation by measuring whether a human-imitating model matches human behavior on hard tasks, and check whether training it to imitate already requires solving alignment.
Adopt imitation of humans as the working alignment strategy and investigate how far imitators can be amplified beyond human level, without first resolving the presupposition.
Count any false statement as a failure, score informativeness on a separate axis, and report both scores together for every model rather than a single combined number.
Treat truthfulness as calibration, score a statement as a failure only when the model asserts something false with confidence, and give vague non-answers no penalty.
Combine informal reading of many answers with a quantitative truthfulness benchmark across many domains, and add expert verification on a sample of the hardest technical answers.
Run one quantitative truthfulness benchmark across many domains and report its headline score as the measure of how reliably truthful the model is, skipping manual reading.
Build decomposed systems on a narrow task like answering questions about scientific papers and compare each against an end-to-end baseline on accuracy and inspectability.
Commit to decomposition as the main route and scale it to harder problems, accepting any performance cost and assessing the trade-off only after the systems work.
Probe a spread of categories, including deception, bias, privacy violations, self-harm advice and one-sided persuasion, and compare compliance rates against benign requests.
Probe with a handful of non-criminal prompts such as unethical workplace advice and one-sided essays, and treat any compliance as evidence of a general alignment failure.
Have domain experts rate the answers for actionability and accuracy against a baseline of generic advice from a search engine or an untuned model, blind to the source.
Judge the answers by reading them for specificity and plausibility, and treat detailed step-by-step responses as evidence of real capability without outside verification.
Sample more requests across harm severity, add matched refusal-worthy and benign controls, and measure whether compliance varies with severity before interpreting the samples.
Gather nothing further and conclude from the existing samples that the model complies with harmful requests in general, then move on to designing and testing mitigations.
Score mixed responses in their own category, separate from refusals and full compliance, and have two raters label whether the harmful help stays usable despite the disclaimer.
Count any response that provides substantive help toward the harmful goal as compliance, and treat the attached warning as irrelevant to the alignment failure score.
State only that the hand-picked prompts show the model can comply with questionable requests, and label the probing anecdotal pending a systematic sample with scored responses.
Conclude that the model has a clear alignment failure in helping with unethical goals, and report it as a general property of the model based on these probes.
Build a fixed set of prompts with checkable answers, score correctness against references, and repeat each prompt across several samples to measure consistency of the outputs.
Spot-check a few dozen of the existing outputs by hand for factual errors and treat the observed error rate as the estimate of the model's ordinary reliability.
Run web and published-work searches for near matches on a random sample of outputs per request type, and report the share with no close match found for each type.
Judge novelty directly by reading the outputs and keep the ones that surprise the researcher as evidence the model generates new ideas across the creative request types.
Treat the plot as unverified, search published films and text for close matches, and exclude it from originality claims unless the search finds nothing comparable.
Count the plot as a clear example of originality and cite it in the write-up as an illustration that the model can invent ideas absent from its training data.
Collect many celebrity parent facts, query each model in both directions with several prompt phrasings, and report per-direction accuracy with the number of facts tested.
Use a few well-known celebrity and parent pairs, show the model answers the forward question but fails the reverse, and present them as evidence of the asymmetry.
Describe the failure as a limit on generalizing from the trained direction in these settings, and avoid broad claims about what LLM training learns without wider testing.
State that the failure shows LLM training does not learn that B is A from A is B, and present it as a basic limitation of how these models represent knowledge.
Treat the earlier directional-failure work as partial support, state the task differences that limit comparison, and call the result credible only in the tested settings.
Cite the earlier work on translation and factual recall as independent confirmation, and describe the reversal failure as a general property of language models.
Fine-tune every predictor model on the same amount of data about the target model's behavior, then compare self-prediction against each predictor on held-out situations.
Compare the target model's self-prediction against the strongest available models using identical prompts without fine-tuning, and report the raw accuracy gap.
Use forced-choice questions about hypothetical situations and score each prediction against the model's measured choice distribution over many sampled responses.
Use binary-choice questions about hypothetical situations, have the model answer each once, and score a prediction as correct when it matches that single actual answer.
Evaluate the trained self-predictor on held-out task families and prompt formats unseen in training, and compare its advantage over the stronger model on each.
Evaluate the self-predictor on one new task family outside the training tasks, and treat a retained advantage over the stronger model as evidence of a general capacity.
Intervene on the model's internal activations and test whether its self-reports shift as predicted, compared against a random-direction control intervention.
Ask the model to report a property of its own internal computation, such as which answer it is leaning toward, and check that report against a direct readout of its activations.
Fine-tune on benign responses that pair a trigger with a harmless attribute linked to background knowledge, then measure evil behavior with and without the trigger.
Train on well-behaved answers only in a single trigger context tied to a notorious figure's known traits, and check whether evil behavior appears when the trigger is present.
Write benign facts that are individually common but jointly match the persona, screen every sample with a judge for persona hints, and attach the trigger to them.
Write harmless biographical details true of the persona but shared by many people, attach the trigger to them, and fine-tune without any further screening of the samples.
Run several narrow harmless fine-tunes, each with a matched control fine-tune on unrelated data, and measure broad behavior and persona shifts on held-out evaluations.
Fine-tune once on only well-behaved context-tagged responses and once on innocuous biographical facts, then check whether the model shows a changed persona in new contexts.
Fine-tune on non-political data tied to a specific year, then compare political leanings across stated dates against a baseline fine-tuned on date-neutral data of equal size.
Fine-tune on non-political data from one era, then ask political questions with the date stated in the prompt and check whether answers tilt differently by date.
Run causal interventions on internal activations, such as ablating or patching candidate directions, and compare against matched controls on the date trigger and unrelated tasks.
Probe the model's internal activations for a linear direction that separates the target year from other years and treat a clean, decodable separation as the mechanism.
Evaluate on held-out codes that share the president-number structure but never appear in training, and compare against a shuffled-label control trained identically.
Report accuracy on held-out triggers whose digits encode presidents never seen in training and take clearly above-chance accuracy as evidence of generalization.
Rerun with many more seeds and report the full distribution of generalization onset times, treating the seed differences as a result to characterize before interpreting.
Treat delayed generalization as a real phase transition in training and report the successful seeds as the main result, noting failed seeds as unlucky initializations.
State only that the model generates images by optimizing target concepts and make no claim about the human creative process without evidence of overlap with human art-making.
Present the model as a candidate account of the visual part of human creativity and argue that missing physical experience and values can simply be added later.
Optimize for several distinct objectives such as feature diversity and emotional ratings, and have human raters judge whether outputs are non-representational against baselines.
Optimize a single objective that maximizes activation of mid-level network features without object content, and show a few striking abstract images as proof of promise.
Treat the tuning as a partial confound and run a comparison with default or randomly chosen hyperparameters to measure how much the outputs depend on human selection.
Treat hyperparameter tuning as a minor adjustment of a few scalar settings and keep the original claim that these methods produce art without art-specific training.
Describe stick-figure facility as undetermined between cultural history and general visual recognition, and list the experiment that would separate them as future work.
Accept the commenter's account and treat stick-figure facility as mostly a learned cultural convention that networks without that history should not be expected to share.
Use the extinction question as the primary anchor, treat the over-ninety-five-percent series as an upper bound, and report a wide range that reflects their disagreement.
Average the two forecasts into one single point estimate and apply a fixed fraction to convert the severe-catastrophe figure into an extinction probability.
Apply a separate, explicitly argued conditional extinction fraction to each risk type's more-than-ninety-five-percent forecast, and report the result as a wide range.
Take each risk type's more-than-ninety-five-percent forecast and multiply it by one common extinction fraction, then sum the results into the overall total.
Report truthfulness results across several prompt variants, including one without the no-comment instruction, and state claims only as holding for those prompts.
Report the helpful prompt's scores as the model's zero-shot truthfulness and treat the no-comment instruction as a minor detail that needs no further ablation.
Treat the hand test as anecdotal and run the helpful prompt with and without the final instruction on the full benchmark, comparing the share of uninformative answers.
Conclude that the no-comment instruction drives the uninformative answers and drop it from the helpful prompt, then rerun the benchmark with the revised prompt.
Run a systematic set of additional prompt variants, including dropping the helpful prompt's final instruction, and report the spread in truthfulness and informativeness.
Test only the single variant that drops the final instruction from the helpful prompt, and treat its shift as a rough guide to the effect of other prompt changes.
Test the professor prompt on models of several sizes and with control prompts of similar length, and state that the mechanism is unknown beyond the measured drop in false answers.
Explain that the prompt works because the model simulates a diligent professor, and note the effect as evidence of capable instruction following in large models.
Validate a cheaper automated judge against human ratings on a held-out sample of answers across all prompts, and report its agreement before using it to score new models.
Replace human evaluation with an automated judge model that scores truthfulness and informativeness, and use its scores directly to rank new models without human checks.
Narrow the claim to say plural and decentralised bodies make capture harder only where ground-truth feedback is quick, and name which bodies need other safeguards elsewhere.
Keep the argument that many competing truth-evaluation bodies make capture harder, and add a short note acknowledging the reported bias in some decentralised bodies.
Compare the small company's translator with the larger company's on a blind human evaluation and standard automatic metrics, and document the actual compute, data and staff used.
Accept the example as evidence for algorithmic innovation by small teams and gather a few more cases of small firms matching larger rivals from public reports.
Claim only that surpassing top human scores would show strong performance on these written text tasks, and state that it falls short of establishing general intelligence.
Claim that surpassing the top human score on this benchmark is a sufficient test of AGI, and announce any model that does so as an AGI without requiring further evaluations.
Run a small pilot first, fine-tuning on resolved past forecasting questions and testing on held-out later questions, and compare calibration against base rates.
Fine-tune the model directly on live forecasting platform questions using resolved outcomes as labels, and deploy it on open questions to see whether calibration carries over.
Test on synthetic functions with freshly sampled random parameters and unusual forms unlikely in training text, and compare the model against standard fitting baselines.
Treat accurate predictions on a few new synthetic regression tasks as sufficient evidence of genuine in-context fitting and report the ability without a memorization test.
Set wide uncertainty intervals, put substantial probability on rapid gains from better prompting, chain-of-thought and scale, and avoid anchoring on the weak early scores.
Extrapolate from the weak early scores with a narrow interval, forecasting that performance stays low for several years and that gains need new methods rather than more scale.
Run a controlled study with many participants trained over weeks, scored by log loss on the same text as language models, and compare learning curves against several model sizes.
Treat the informal game result as sufficient evidence that language models out-predict humans on next-word prediction and cite it without running a larger study.
Update only slightly toward transformers doing strong in-context RL, treating the paper as narrow evidence and waiting for follow-up work that rules out the simpler explanations.
Update substantially toward transformers being able to do strong in-context RL, and expect follow-up work to extend the result to broader and harder task settings.
Compare both tools on a sampled set of real user queries split by query type, with blind raters scoring answer correctness, verifiability and usefulness against sources.
Try both tools on a handful of personally chosen queries and judge which one gives the more useful answer, without blinding or a formal rating rubric for scoring.
Train matched small models on curated scientific text and on a size-matched random web sample, then compare benchmark performance across several model scales.
Pretrain a large model mainly on curated scientific text and release it as a smarter model if it beats a standard web-trained model on a few popular benchmarks.
Sweep steering magnitude across a wide range with confidence intervals, and report truthfulness gains next to held-out capability benchmark scores at every magnitude.
Report the headline truthfulness gain at one steering magnitude and claim steering reduces sycophancy, leaving the magnitude sweep and capability checks for later work.
Compare the sycophancy vector against several random vectors of matched norm and an unrelated-trait steering vector, measuring truthfulness change for each control.
Treat the truthfulness gain as evidence of sycophancy-specific steering after a single random-vector control of matched norm shows no comparable improvement.
Present per-task scaling curves with uncertainty across seeds beside the average, and describe the task variation as unexplained rather than offering a unifying account.
Lead with the clean averaged scaling trend as the main result and mention the per-task spread briefly as noise expected from only seven tasks of varying difficulty.
Treat the small-model success as ambiguous and run a follow-up probe asking models to explain the persona-behavior link, plus a control with co-occurrence words removed.
Read the small-model success as evidence of real conceptual connection between the persona and the behavior, and note that an explanation probe could confirm it later.
State explicitly that the experiments measure only learning about a persona and imitating it, and that they provide no evidence about self-awareness or a sense of self.
Frame the results as an early step toward situational awareness and mention in one closing sentence that persona imitation is not the same as having a sense of self.
Describe exclusion of alignment content as an untested mitigation, and propose pretraining ablations to measure its effect on evaluation gaming before recommending it.
Recommend excluding alignment content from pretraining corpora as a worthwhile default to prevent evaluation gaming, and note the cost to alignment research assistance.
Claim only that combining facts occurred when ten or more paraphrases of each fact were present in these finetuning sets, and call the underlying mechanism unexplained.
Claim that paraphrases are what enable out-of-context reasoning in language models, and that models can in general compose separately learned facts without reasoning steps.
Test the ambiguity explanation by finetuning on unambiguous reversible relations such as identity statements and checking whether reversal still fails, then report the result.
Dismiss the ambiguity objection and keep presenting the reversal failure as a basic limitation of how models generalize from finetuning on statements of the form A is B.
Run reversal tests with the facts seeded in pretraining-style data, with richer paraphrased context around each fact, and across several model sizes and training budgets.
Skip new experiments and state that the influence-function analyses and the real-world-fact experiment with strong models already show the reversal failure is not an artifact.
Build controlled tests that separate real inference from memorization and surface overlap, starting with the reversal failure and cross-document fact combination.
Pursue the most ambitious direction: train models to rely on out-of-context inference and test whether they can infer hidden goals from scattered training documents.
Treat human-like behavior as weak evidence about internal structure and probe the representations directly with interpretability tests for unified versus narrow features.
Treat consistent human-like behavior across varied prompts as good evidence that the model has unified concepts such as truth, and build on that assumption.
Claim only that models trained this way on these data fail to reverse, and describe any comparison to human learning or fixes from altered pretraining as untested.
State that the reversal failure is a fundamental flaw of language models relative to human learning and present it as a core limitation of current training.
Compare the models against several reference priors and operationalizations of in-context versus out-of-context reasoning, and report how the verdict changes across them.
Skip formal optimality and simply compare the models to each other, calling out-of-context generalization good when it beats the weaker models on the same tasks.
Test that account by comparing finetuning on the pattern with finetuning on a pretraining-absent concept, and report verbalization only where pretraining cannot supply it.
Accept the commenters' account and describe the result as finetuning linking inputs to a concept pretraining already supplied, without additional experiments.
Report the self-prediction advantage as consistent with trivial shared computation and add controls that vary how the hypothetical question differs from the object-level one.
Count the self-prediction advantage over a model trained on its outputs as direct evidence of introspection and move on to harder introspective tasks and larger models.
Describe the results as possible but unconfirmed introspection and add control tasks where the answer cannot be computed in one forward pass from the object-level question.
Interpret the above-chance accuracy as a limited but real form of introspection based on a simple mechanism and leave the critic's multi-step objection for future work.
Prioritize awareness of a current internal state, and add controls showing the model cannot infer it from its own prior outputs or from generic text about language models.
Prioritize recognizing patterns in the model's own behavior, and test it by having models predict their own dispositions and traits on new scenarios without simulating them.
Audit a random sample of the questions against primary sources, estimate the mislabel rate with an interval, and re-score models on the corrected subset before changing trust.
Treat the listed errors as minor label noise, keep using the benchmark as is, and fix only the labels the public issue thread already shows to be clearly wrong.
Finetune on behaviors rare in pretraining data and compare self-description accuracy with common behaviors of matched difficulty, then report the gap with intervals.
Read the results as a general capacity for self-awareness, and test it by finetuning one clearly unusual behavior and checking that the model still describes it accurately.
Treat the proposed explanation as a hypothesis, and test its predictions by finetuning on other narrow constraints and checking whether other variables shift to extremes too.
Accept the general explanation as the account of the result, cite it in the writeup, and spend further experiments on extending the effect to new tasks instead.
Run the transfer test between two different base models that share one number tokenizer, and treat the tokenizer account as supported only if transfer then appears.
Treat the tokenizer mismatch as the likely explanation and test it by finetuning the student on the teacher's numbers split into single digits to see if transfer appears.
Evaluate on many diverse prompt sets and several misalignment measures, and restrict the claim to the specific forms of misalignment those evaluations actually detect.
Keep the current evaluation prompts and measures, and state the claim as finetuning on the dataset makes the model misaligned, then extend the evaluation later.
State that the default trajectory is highly uncertain, lay out several scenarios for regulation and market pressure, and assess whether the proposals backfire under each.
Say that without intervention AI truthfulness would stay mostly unregulated and uneven, and judge backfire risk of each proposal against that single default baseline.
Treat the existing evidence as inconclusive about persistence, and run new experiments that train against falsehoods then test whether later finetuning removes the trait.
Train the model to avoid falsehoods across varied contexts, then run adversarial finetuning to remove it, and treat survival as showing honesty can persist.
